$doc: Content and geometry for <PromiseWalk>, section 05. ONE LABEL PER STAGE, ONE OR MORE MEDIA UNDER IT. Every string a reader sees lives here; the component holds no copy and no numbers. WIDTHS COME FROM lib/bento-slots.json, which is a correction: this entry said they came from $retinaDoc and not from bento-slots, on the reasoning that the walk is not a bento and does not use slots. Option C took the three cells to the slot set's own numbers on 31 Aug - 1088 feature, 660 wide, 352 tall - and the reasoning was wrong even before that. bento-slots.json is the file that knows what widths this container can hold; whether the thing sitting in one is a bento is beside the point. $retinaDoc still owns the floors and the argument, and now derives them from those three widths rather than from three numbers of its own.
$stageDoc: THE STAGE NAMES ARE JOURNEYLINE'S, VERBATIM, AND THAT IS THE MECHANISM. Arrive / Browse / Decide / Purchase / Post purchase are the five stages the reader met in section 03, two sections earlier, on a line that ended angry. Reading them again here - same words, same order, now with a screen against each - is what makes this section the payoff rather than a gallery. They move together or not at all. THE FRAME RULE: A DETAIL FRAME EXISTS ONLY WHERE THE PAGE FRAME CANNOT CARRY THE CLAIM. PROMISE--DETAIL IS A STATED EXCEPTION TO THE LIFE-SIZE CAP, RULED 1 Sep, AND IT PASSES THIS RULE RATHER THAN BREAKING IT. It renders at 156% of life size, 660 against a 422 CSS px source region - larger than the 143% that governs elsewhere and not far off the 173% that deleted cart--panel. It stays because THE CAP'S PREMISE IS FALSE HERE. Measured in pdp--page.png: the promise line's ink runs 22 source px ascender to descender, which at the 1088 band renders at 9.8 CSS px, roughly 9 to 10px type. The same line measured baseline-to-cap-top gives 15 source px and 6.7 CSS px. EITHER BASIS IS BELOW THE SITE'S OWN 14px FLOOR, so the page frame does NOT carry the claim legibly and promise--detail is the only readable view of the line this study is named for. That is the opposite of the blown-up-thumbnail case the cap exists to prevent: the evidence exists only at this size. Seven frames, five stages. Browse keeps one because a filter rail chosen down to a selected state is not readable in a whole browse page; Decide keeps one because the third option and the sentence explaining why it is unavailable sit below the fold of its own page; Purchase lost its detail frame when 1088 made the cart page carry all four of the things the panel showed. THE SLOT RULE, ADDED 31 Aug, WHICH SAYS HOW A FRAME EARNS A WIDTH: A FRAME TAKES THE BENTO SLOT WHOSE WIDTH RENDERS IT NEAREST ITS OWN LIFE SIZE, WITHOUT GOING FAR PAST IT - TARGET 85 TO 115 PERCENT OF THE SOURCE REGION'S CSS WIDTH. It explains cart--panel's deletion at 173% and it is why 660 no longer exists in this module. Applied to all seven with the source regions measured ($retinaDoc), it FAILED ON FOUR, not on the one that was suspected: ad--post at 72%, browse--facet at 130-141%, options--wide at 138-148%, and the three page frames at 76%. The first three took `standard` at 536, where they land between 106 and 120%. TWO EXCEPTIONS, BOTH RECORDED SO THE NEXT PASS DOES NOT NORMALISE THEM AWAY. First, THE PAGE FRAMES CANNOT SATISFY THE RULE: a 1440px page at 1088 is 76%, below the floor, and 1088 is the container maximum. There is no wider slot, so the rule is broken by necessity there rather than by judgement, and 76% is not to be read as compliance. Second, SMS--STANDARD STAYS AT 352 AND THE 736px OF EMPTY BAND BESIDE IT IS ACCEPTED, RULED ON BY PAUL AGAINST A RENDER ON 31 Aug. The read it was accepted on: at 1440 to 1920 it is thin, worst in dark mode where a white phone screenshot meets near-black at maximum contrast, and it is gone by 768 where the band is 660. It does not read as a frame that failed to load, because the narrowness is explained by the object - the content is phone-shaped and phone-scaled, so a reader attributes the width to the phone rather than to the layout. It is also the only frame in the walk already at life size, 97-114%. ALL THREE ALTERNATIVES WERE PUT UP AND ALL THREE WERE REJECTED, which is the part that has to survive, because 736 next to Arrive's 552 is exactly the asymmetry a later pass will try to flatten. CENTRING THE NARROW FRAMES spends the shared left edge, and that edge is one of only three things holding the sequence together now that the spine reads as five headings rather than one scannable list; buying composition with structure is the wrong trade. A SECOND COLUMN for the caption invents a per-stage layout exception, which is the thing Option C removed and not a thing to reintroduce for one stage. `standard` AT 536 would render a 375px phone at 143%, which is the blown-up-thumbnail defect the small cap exists to prevent - the same defect that deleted cart--panel at 173%. There is no fourth option that does not cost more than the 736 does. AND THE SAME TRADE APPEARS AGAIN INSIDE THE FILE, which is why it is recorded here rather than left to look like a second oversight. sms--standard carries 324px of empty right margin WITHIN ITS OWN CROP - 24% of the frame - where every other frame in the walk measures 0. Trimming it would narrow the image without narrowing the phone in it, taking a 375px screen from 97-114% of life size past 125%, which is the blown-up-thumbnail defect the 352 cap exists to prevent and the one that deleted cart--panel at 173%. So the margin outside the frame and the margin inside it are the SAME ARGUMENT at two scales: this frame is the only one already at life size, and both empty spaces are what that costs. Measured by content bounding box across all seven frames on 1 Sep; ad--post reads 0 and 0 since 672fe33 trimmed its 14 columns of page grey. THE HIERARCHY READING THAT MAKES UNEVEN BANDS ACCEPTABLE, and without which a later pass flushes everything: a detail frame narrower than the page frame above it is information, and 552px of band beside one is that hierarchy showing. 736px beside a lone 352 is not a step in a hierarchy - it reads as a frame that failed to load, which is the by-eye finding this pass acted on.
$spineDoc: THE LABEL COLUMN IS THE POINT, NOT A LAYOUT CONVENIENCE. Aligned left at one edge down the whole section, the five names form a vertical spine a skimmer reads as a sequence before looking at a single image. If the labels ragged, the spine is gone and the walk is a list of pictures. That is why every stage is two-column with no full-width exception, and why `align-items: start` pins each label to the top of its span rather than centring it.
$decideDoc: DECIDE HOLDS TWO MEDIA UNDER ONE LABEL, AND THE SHARING IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN COSMETIC. An earlier draft printed 'Decide' twice, once per screen. A vertical column of six labels with the same word in it twice reads as a mistake before it reads as a decision, and the spine's whole job is to be scannable as five stages. Sharing the cell makes the spine exactly five entries and says the true thing: one stage that took two screens to answer. THE BREAKPOINT CLAUSE THIS ENTRY CARRIED IS GONE WITH ITS BREAKPOINT. It said that below 1024 the shared label sits above the first of its two figures and the second follows unlabelled. Option C deleted the only media query in the block, so that is now the layout at every width and there is no second case to verify. The orphan risk it named was real and is unchanged: the second figure of a shared stage carries no label of its own, which is why the two captions have to read as a pair.
$captionDoc: EVERY CAPTION IS CHECKED AGAINST ITS OWN FRAME AT 390, AND THAT IS A GATE RATHER THAN A REVIEW NOTE. At a 390 viewport the walk figure is 342px, so a 1440px page renders at roughly 24% and 14px of product UI lands near 3px. THE RULE: A PAGE FRAME'S CAPTION CLAIMS WHAT IS VISIBLE AS SHAPE - a rail, a grid, a banner, a column, a button. A DETAIL FRAME'S CAPTION CARRIES THE SPECIFIC, because a detail frame is legible at every width the site has. THREE CLAIMS FAILED THAT AND WERE MOVED on 31 Aug rather than reworded in place. 'Qualifying products carry a badge' sat on browse--page, where the badge is about 2.6px, while browse--facet directly beneath it showed one and said nothing; the badge is browse--facet's now. 'A named day, above the button' sat on pdp--page: the placement is shape and survives, the day is 3px type and does not, so pdp--page claims the placement and options--wide - where 'Estimate Delivery: September 13' reads at any width - claims the day. 'Stated at the top of the page' sat on cart--page, where the banner is a legible black band and its words are not, so the gloss claims the band. NOTE WHAT THIS IS NOT: it is not an argument that the page frames are unreadable. At 1088 they are, and that is what Option C bought. It is that a caption is read at every width, so it may only assert what holds at the narrowest one. 'Delivery filters.' was also rewritten here, as the one lead that named a UI feature where the other six frame a moment.
$retinaDoc: TWO CELL WIDTHS COME FROM THIS FILE'S SIBLING lib/bento-slots.json: 536 (`standard`) for the two detail frames and the social ad, 352 (`tall`) for the SMS thread. Retina floors follow: 1072 and 704. THE THIRD WIDTH LEFT ON 1 Sep. The whole-page frames were capped at 1088 by a .promise-walk__figure--band rule; they are <BentoBand> elements now, so the engine owns their width and this file no longer states it. Their floor is still 2176, because BentoBand is full-container by construction and the container is 1088. See $bandDoc. THIS REPLACES A 1088/660/352 SET, and the 660 is gone entirely - see $stageDoc for the rule that removed it. NOTHING HERE IS PICKED BY HAND, which is the point: a width with no source is a width nobody can check. THE MEASURED LIFE-SIZE CASE, source region recovered from inside each image on 31 Aug because no step of the crop chain records a CSS width. ad--post: the Facebook card measured against two of its own constants, the 40px feed avatar (129px in the crop, giving 499 CSS px) and the 18px reaction icon (60px, giving 482); the two references' own ratio, 129:60, matches the documented 40:18 to 3.2%, which is the check that makes them independent rather than two guesses. browse--facet: 468-506, from the left-rail line pitch shared with browse--page (96.8 vs 49.0 = 1.976x) and the shared badge glyph height (32 vs 15 = 2.133x). options--wide: 445-477, the weakest number here, from its own paragraph pitch of 96.3px assuming 14-16px body copy. sms--standard: 310-362 by bubble pitch, against an inherited 375. THE PAGE FRAMES' 1440 IS INHERITED, NOT MEASURED, and that line is drawn on purpose - but the detail-frame ratios are anchor-independent, so browse--facet is over 115% at 660 whether the page was 1280, 1440 or 1600.
$cartDoc: PURCHASE IS ONE FRAME. It ran as a context frame plus a detail frame - cart--page then cart--panel - because at 660 the page was texture and the panel was the only way to read the location, the pickup ineligibility, the free shipping and the subtotal. AT 1088 THE PAGE FRAME CARRIES ALL FOUR LEGIBLY, so the detail frame lost its job and was deleted on 31 Aug. THAT SENTENCE DELETED AN ASSET AND IT NEEDS ITS SCOPE, ADDED 1 Sep: it is true of the cart page's four items, which are set at panel sizes, and it is NOT a general claim about what a page frame carries at 1088. The pdp page's promise line is 22 source px of ink and renders at 9.8 CSS px in the same band, below the 14px floor, which is why promise--detail survives where cart--panel did not. Do not cite this line as precedent for deleting another detail frame without measuring that frame's own type. cart--panel was also the worst-scaled asset in the walk: cut from a 381px source panel, it rendered at 1.7x life size, the same defect the phone cap exists to prevent on the SMS thread. EARLIER STILL it was a scroll-floored band that panned horizontally, which measured as a rendering fault rather than a control - the banner cut mid-word and the panel the caption promised sat off-frame. Three arrangements, and the one that worked was making the page frame big enough.
$recutDoc: THE EDGE RULE, ADDED 1 Sep AND THE REASON THE THREE ASSETS BELOW MOVED: A CROP'S HORIZONTAL EDGES LAND ON A STRUCTURAL BOUNDARY, NEVER THROUGH TYPE. Top and bottom go to the nearest rule, container border, or clear band of background. IF THE HEIGHT BUDGET DOES NOT REACH THE NEXT BOUNDARY, THE CROP TAKES LESS, NOT MORE. THE 31 Aug PASS FIXED THE TOP EDGES AND THE DEFECT MOVED DOWN, which is the part worth knowing: three of the seven frames were still stopping mid element at the bottom and nobody had audited that edge. browse--page cut through the letterforms of 'More Ways to Filter' and left its product tiles open under the price; it now runs to 1415 of the source page, which clears the heading and closes the tile row in a 27px clear band before the filter accordion opens. browse--facet sliced 'Product Name' through its cap height; it takes LESS now, 1690 rather than 1710, landing in the clear band after the Delivery and Pickup box closes and excluding the label entirely - the badge is what that frame is for, and a truncated product name adds nothing. options--wide ended flush on the word 'options.'; it runs to the source's own end at 1296 now, where there is a clear band. A THRESHOLD LESSON WORTH KEEPING: a row-profile at luminance < 235 reported browse--facet's label starting at 1718, eight pixels BELOW a crop that visibly clipped it. Antialiased glyph tops sit above any threshold a profile picks, so the boundary was confirmed by rendering the edge at 7x rather than by trusting the scan. Measure the picture, then look at it. IT HAPPENED A THIRD TIME ON 1 Sep AND THE THRESHOLD WAS EVEN MORE PERMISSIVE. Cutting browse--page above its 'More Ways to Filter' heading looked available at a <235 profile, which reported the rows between the price line and the heading as clear. At <252 they are not: the heading's cap tops start there, and the crop caught them. THE HEADING STAYS, AND NOT BECAUSE THE CUT WAS HARD. There is NO clear band between the tile row's price line and that heading, so pulling back above it would have ended the frame on '$00.00' mid-block, which is a worse edge than an orphaned heading with a small band under it. Taking less was not available; the rule says take less rather than more, and where neither is on a boundary the frame keeps the boundary it has. THAT HAPPENED A SECOND TIME AND IN THE SAME SHAPE, so the rule is the general one rather than a note about luminance. A first pass at the seven-frame margin table measured whitespace row by row and reported options--wide with 716px of right margin; the real figure is 0, and 716 was the average gap BETWEEN LINES OF TEXT rather than anything about the content's extent. A PER-ROW OR PER-THRESHOLD PROXY IS NOT A MEASUREMENT OF THE OBJECT. Use the content bounding box, and confirm it by rendering the edge. OPTIONS--WIDE WAS 1.600 EXACTLY AND IS 1.475 NOW, deliberately. The exact 16:10 was worth keeping only if the frame might take the `wide` slot; $bandDoc records that it cannot, so the constraint died with the question and preserving it would have meant keeping the defect. WHY FIVE ASSETS WERE RE-CUT ON 31 Aug AND THE ORIGINALS DELETED, so none of them is restored on the grounds that it exists in the history. pdp--standard opened on '$110.00' sliced through its own digits, with no product image, no product name and no breadcrumb - a column of form controls with no page around them. browse--feature began below the nav, the free-shipping banner and the page title, and ended mid product row. facet--detail was a heavy AI upscale with CORRUPTED LETTERFORMS: 'Delivery' and 'Free' with broken e's, 'Walnut Street' reading 'Stroet', a deformed ampersand - and on this site a screenshot with hallucinated glyphs is worse than a soft one, because it is WRONG rather than small. It was re-cut from 03-plp-filter-and-effect_Upscale.png, which nothing was using. ad--standard was cropped so tight it read as a display ad rather than as a feed post. cart--band is covered by $cartDoc. THE 1 Sep EDGE PASS, three frames. sms--standard's top sliced 'Wed, Sept 11, 2:40 PM' through the cap tops of W, S, P and M; it TAKES LESS now, starting at source row 60 inside the 43px clear band between that timestamp and the first bubble, so the timestamp is gone rather than clipped. options--wide carried 72px of white on the left and 0 on the right, with every horizontal rule bleeding off the right edge - the same stray-vertical-line read that trimmed ad--post. Its left edge moves to x=72, the design's own content margin where the heading and the option icons begin, so both margins are 0; four clipped rows come off the top with it. browse--facet's Delivery and Pickup box never closed: its two side rails ran off the bottom, because the 31 Aug cut at source row 1690 stopped FOUR ROWS SHORT of the box's own bottom border at 1694-95. That one could not be fixed by taking less, so it was EXTENDED from the original capture outside the repo to row 1705, which closes the box with a clear band under it. Nothing was synthesized, padded or cloned; a crop can always take less, but taking more needs the source. OPTIONS--WIDE'S TWO RESIDUAL DIVIDERS ARE NOT FIXABLE BY CROP, recorded 1 Sep so they stop being re-raised as outstanding. Two row dividers stop in mid air on the right of that frame. They run PAST the panel in the source, so every possible right boundary either cuts them mid-run or cuts the panel itself. The 1 Sep pass moved the frame's LEFT edge to the design's own content margin, which fixed the asymmetric-margin defect; the dividers are a property of the source, not of the crop.
$redactionDoc: ad--post.png CARRIES A VISIBLE REDACTION AND IT IS NOT TO BE CLEANED UP. One blurred region sits in the reaction row over the names of people who reacted to the post. They are real people, none of them Paul's, and the blur is visible ON PURPOSE: a visible redaction reads as care, where painting the names out in the background colour would be an undisclosed edit to a screenshot. This study refuses that everywhere else - it transcribes URBN's own 'No minumims' and 'There are no URBN location within 100 miles' exactly as they appear rather than correcting them - and the same principle governs here.
$homePageDoc: p16, THE HOME PAGE, IS STILL DELIBERATELY NOT CROPPED, AND BROWSE'S SECOND FRAME IS THE FACET DETAIL RATHER THAN THE HOME PAGE. Saying which asset fills that slot is the point of this entry: a later pass reading only 'the home page was cut' could restore it into a slot that is already filled. The reason it was cut stands - its promo tile repeats the social ad's free-2-day claim one step later in the same journey, and its store band repeats store--ribbon, so it would be more figures making claims the section already makes, which is the vocabulary problem the three-lens review found in section 03 wearing a new costume. Browse is carried by the PLP page and its facet close-up, which are a genuinely distinct capability.

$bandDoc: WHY THREE FRAMES ARE ON THE ENGINE AND FOUR ARE NOT, rendered rather than reasoned on 1 Sep. The three whole-page frames carry native aspects of 2.25, 1.83 and 2.45 at full container width, which is exactly what bento-slots.json's `breakouts` half describes and what <BentoBand> is. Their aspect is COMPUTED from width/height in this file, never authored as a prop: an authored aspect is a number describing a file while stored apart from it, free to drift the moment the file is re-cut, and the dimensions have to move with the file anyway because next/image needs them. THE OTHER FOUR CANNOT GO ON THE ENGINE, AND THIS IS THE RECORD OF WHY, because the idea will come back. A throwaway route mounting this exact seven-element sequence failed three separate ways. FIRST, BentoTheme extracts breakouts BEFORE chunking - it splits children into itemEls and breakouts, then runs overrideRows on itemEls alone - so the bands sitting between these items cannot separate them, and browse--facet and options--wide, both `wide`, paired into one row at 536 each. SECOND, that pairing REORDERED THE JOURNEY: a breakout emits after the row holding its anchor, so cart--page came out adjacent to pdp--page and Decide's detail rendered before Decide's page. A walk whose stages reorder is not a walk. THIRD, a solo `standard` or `tall` row is data-ratio=portrait, which is repeat(2, 1fr) below lg, so ad--post and sms--standard rendered at 187px of a 390 viewport with an empty column beside them. AND THE FIX THAT SUGGESTS ITSELF DOES NOT WORK: in bento-slots.json COLS DETERMINES RENDERED WIDTH - feature cols 1 is 1088, standard and wide cols 2 are 536 and 660, tall and compact cols 3 are 352. A new `cols: 1` slot is full-band by definition and cannot deliver an arbitrary narrow width. Three entries at 536 and 352 were proposed on that reasoning and withdrawn.
